# Select: `jl-select`

A choice among a list, on the browser's own select.

- Class `JlSelect`, an atom: `import { JlSelect } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/select

A choice among a list, on the browser's own select: the keyboard works as people expect, the form
gets the chosen value, and on a touch screen the list opens the way the platform does it (a sheet on phones). With a
mouse, in the browsers that let a page draw a select's list (Chrome, Edge), it looks like the combobox's: the same
panel, rows and check; the others show their own.

Give the choices as JSON in options (an option with a group goes under that heading), or write option and optgroup
elements inside the element, as for a native select: they are copied in when it connects. A placeholder shows
while nothing is chosen and cannot be picked back; with required, it stops the submission.

## Use

```ts
import { JlSelect } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlSelect
  label="Region"
  options={[{"group":"Europe","label":"Frankfurt","value":"eu-central"},{"group":"Europe","label":"Zurich","value":"eu-south"},{"group":"Americas","label":"Virginia","value":"us-east"},{"group":"Americas","label":"Oregon","value":"us-west"},{"disabled":true,"group":"Asia","label":"Tokyo (full)","value":"ap-north"}]}
  placeholder="Choose a region"
/>
```

```html
<jl-select
  label="Region"
  options='[{"group":"Europe","label":"Frankfurt","value":"eu-central"},{"group":"Europe","label":"Zurich","value":"eu-south"},{"group":"Americas","label":"Virginia","value":"us-east"},{"group":"Americas","label":"Oregon","value":"us-west"},{"disabled":true,"group":"Asia","label":"Tokyo (full)","value":"ap-north"}]'
  placeholder="Choose a region"
></jl-select>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `options` (attribute `options`): `SelectOption<Value>[]`, default `[]`. The choices; empty: the option elements written inside are used.
- `value` (attribute `value`): `Value | ''`, default `''`. The chosen value. One that no option has (a choice since removed, options still loading) shows as an option of its own, first, and the form keeps it.
- `placeholder` (attribute `placeholder`): `string`, default `''`. Shown while nothing is chosen; it cannot be picked back.
- `size` (attribute `size`): `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`, default `'md'`. The height.
- `name` (attribute `name`): `string`, default `''`. The field's name in the form's data.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The accessible name, when no visible label names the field.
- `required` (attribute `required`): `boolean`, default `false`. The form cannot be submitted while the placeholder shows.
- `disabled` (attribute `disabled`): `boolean`, default `false`. Cannot be changed or focused.
- `invalid` (attribute `invalid`): `boolean`, default `false`. Drawn in the danger colour, for an error the page found.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `change` (`onChange` in JSX), detail `Value`: Someone chose an option.

## Slots

- The default slot: option and optgroup elements, copied into the select when no options are given.

## Methods

- `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`: Focuses the native select.
- `checkValidity(): boolean`: Whether a required select has a choice.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The frame around the select.

## Typing

Typed by its values, JlSelect<'chf' | 'eur'> takes options of those values only, and gives change and value as one of them: the editor completes them and refuses another. In JSX, the type can also be read from the options. Options written in HTML, as JSON or <option> children, are not checked.

```ts
import type { JlSelect } from '@syware/jlib';

type Currency = 'chf' | 'eur';

const currency = document.querySelector<JlSelect<Currency>>('jl-select.currency');
currency?.options.set([
  { label: 'Swiss franc', value: 'chf' },
  { label: 'Euro', value: 'eur' },
]);
// @ts-expect-error: 'usd' is not a currency of the list
currency?.options.set([{ label: 'US dollar', value: 'usd' }]);
currency?.events.register('change', (value) => setCurrency(value)); // value: Currency
```

```tsx
import { Jadis } from '@jadis/core';
import { JlSelect } from '@syware/jlib';

import type { SelectOption } from '@syware/jlib';

type Currency = 'chf' | 'eur';

const CURRENCIES: SelectOption<Currency>[] = [
  { label: 'Swiss franc', value: 'chf' },
  { label: 'Euro', value: 'eur' },
];

export class InvoiceForm extends Jadis {
  static readonly selector = 'invoice-form';

  templateHtml(): Node {
    // value="usd" does not compile. Without <Currency>, the type is read from the options.
    return (
      <JlSelect<Currency>
        label="Currency"
        options={CURRENCIES}
        value="chf"
        onChange={(value) => setCurrency(value)}
      />
    );
  }
}

InvoiceForm.register();
```

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### From JSON, with groups

Options with a group gather under its heading; a disabled one shows but cannot be chosen.

```html
<div class="narrow">
  <jl-select
    label="Region"
    placeholder="Choose a region"
    options='[{"group":"Europe","label":"Frankfurt","value":"eu-central"},{"group":"Europe","label":"Zurich","value":"eu-south"},{"group":"Americas","label":"Virginia","value":"us-east"},{"group":"Americas","label":"Oregon","value":"us-west"},{"disabled":true,"group":"Asia","label":"Tokyo (full)","value":"ap-north"}]'
  ></jl-select>
</div>
```

### From option elements

Written as for a native select; the selected option is the value.

```html
<div class="narrow">
  <jl-select label="Time zone" value="Europe/Zurich">
    <optgroup label="Europe">
      <option value="Europe/London">London</option>
      <option value="Europe/Zurich">Zurich</option>
    </optgroup>
    <optgroup label="Asia">
      <option value="Asia/Tokyo">Tokyo</option>
    </optgroup>
  </jl-select>
</div>
```

### Sizes

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-select size="sm" label="Small" value="b" options='[{"value":"a","label":"Small"},{"value":"b","label":"Small, chosen"}]'></jl-select>
  <jl-select label="Medium" options='[{"value":"a","label":"Medium"}]'></jl-select>
  <jl-select size="lg" label="Large" options='[{"value":"a","label":"Large"}]'></jl-select>
</div>
```

### States

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-select label="Disabled" disabled options='[{"value":"a","label":"Disabled"}]'></jl-select>
  <jl-select label="Invalid" invalid placeholder="Nothing chosen" options='[{"value":"a","label":"A"}]'></jl-select>
</div>
```

### Listening

The paragraph listens to change.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-select
    class="demo-sort"
    label="Sort by"
    value="recent"
    options='[{"value":"recent","label":"Most recent"},{"value":"name","label":"Name"},{"value":"size","label":"Size"}]'
  ></jl-select>
  <p class="muted demo-out">Sorted by recent.</p>
</div>
```

```js
const select = root.querySelector('.demo-sort');
const out = root.querySelector('.demo-out');
select.events.register('change', (value) => {
  out.textContent = `Sorted by ${value}.`;
});
```
